## Why Look Beyond Google Docs?

From yesterday's survey of BTS researchers:

- Strong disdain for mega-corps and a preference for open source
- Worries about cost and "adoption then enshittification"
- Frustration with tools that make it impossible to collaborate across institutions
- Want simultaneous editing *and* version history

Google Docs works for a lot of people. But not every collaborator can or wants to use it.

::: notes
Not anti-Google: it's a low-barrier default. The point is to know what the options are when it doesn't fit your team.
:::

## What Is HackMD?

- A real-time collaborative markdown editor in the browser: [hackmd.io](https://hackmd.io/)
- Write on the left, see the formatted result on the right
- Notes are plain text, so they're easy to move, version, and sync with GitHub
- Our working group built its [BTS tools map](https://hackmd.io/K01UHojtQwa_f2H8eOCkqA) in it

::: notes
Open the tools map and switch between the three views with the buttons at the top: edit only, split (edit + preview side by side), and view only. Then show the table of contents and the workflow diagram rendering live.
:::

## Markdown in 60 Seconds

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**You type:**

```markdown
# A heading
## A smaller heading

*italics* and **bold**

- a bullet
- another bullet

> a quote

| Task | Tool |
|------|------|
| Writing | HackMD |
```
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**You see:**

[A heading]{style="font-size:1.4em; font-weight:700; color:#1f3a5f"}

[A smaller heading]{style="font-size:1.1em; font-weight:700; color:#1f3a5f"}

*italics* and **bold**

- a bullet
- another bullet

> a quote

| Task | Tool |
|------|------|
| Writing | HackMD |
:::
::::

::: notes
Markdown is part of the "hidden curriculum": a general skill you pick up once and then use everywhere (GitHub, Quarto, Slack, Discord, many note apps).
:::

## Features That Help Big Teams

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Live co-editing with everyone's cursor visible
- Comments and named notes inline
- Version history to go back in time
- Tables, images, and diagrams (Mermaid)
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
- GitHub sync to push notes to a repo
- Templates for agendas and protocols
- Books that link notes into one guide
- Slide mode to present straight from a note
:::
::::

## A Real Example: Our Workflow Doc

```markdown
### Stage 2 — Study Design & Pre-Registration

> [name=steven verheyen] In the Dutch Open Science Community,
> AsPredicted is very much frowned upon because it isn't
> specific enough.

| Tool | Category | Pricing | Notes |
|------|----------|---------|-------|
| OSF Registries | Preregistration | Free | ... |
```

- `[name=...]` tags each comment with who said it
- The whole working group edited one doc, with no "final_v3_REAL.docx"

[Open the doc](https://hackmd.io/K01UHojtQwa_f2H8eOCkqA)

## What's Free and What Isn't?

| | Free | Prime ($5/seat/month, billed annually) |
|---|---|---|
| Private notes | Yes | Yes |
| Invited editors per note | 3 | Unlimited |
| Team workspace | Up to 3 people | Unlimited seats |
| Version history | Last 10 versions | Unlimited |
| GitHub sync | 20 pushes/month | Unlimited |
| Comments | Yes | Yes |
| Full-text search, PDF export | No | Yes |

[Source: [hackmd.io/pricing](https://hackmd.io/pricing), checked October 2026]{.small}

::: notes
Answers the working group's question "can't do private stuff without paying?": private notes are free. The limit is the number of *invited* editors (3) and team size. For bigger groups, set the note's write permission to signed-in users and share the link. Demo this live.
:::

## Other Ways to Write Together

| Tool | Best for | Open source? | Cost |
|------|----------|--------------|------|
| [HedgeDoc](https://hedgedoc.org/) | HackMD-style markdown you host yourself | Yes | Free (self-hosted) |
| [CryptPad](https://cryptpad.org/) | End-to-end encrypted docs, sheets, and markdown | Yes | Free 1 GB account; paid plans; self-host |
| [Etherpad](https://etherpad.org/) | Lightweight real-time text editing | Yes | Free (self-hosted) |
| [Proton Docs](https://proton.me/drive/docs) | Encrypted rich-text docs that open .docx | No | Free with a Proton account |
| [ONLYOFFICE](https://www.onlyoffice.com/) / [Collabora](https://www.collaboraonline.com/) | Word-like editing, often via Nextcloud | Yes | Free community editions; often institutional |
| [Overleaf](https://www.overleaf.com/) | LaTeX manuscripts | Partly | Free plan: 1 collaborator per project |
| Word online | Track changes, journal formatting | No | Usually institutional |
| [Quarto](https://quarto.org/) + GitHub | Reproducible manuscripts with code | Yes | Free |

::: notes
HedgeDoc is the open-source cousin of HackMD (they share a code history), so it's the closest match if your institution can host it.
:::

## Which One Should My Team Use?

- Do you need tracked changes and journal formatting? → Word, ONLYOFFICE, or Collabora
- Is privacy essential, or are some collaborators unable to use Google? → CryptPad or Proton Docs
- Is your team comfortable with markdown and GitHub? → HackMD or HedgeDoc
- Are you writing a LaTeX paper? → Overleaf
- Do you want code and text in one place? → Quarto + GitHub

Rule of thumb: pick the tool your least technical collaborator can use.

## Tips for Big Team Writing

- Keep one source of truth: draft in one place, finalize in one place
- Draft in HackMD, finalize elsewhere: move to Word or Quarto for journal formatting
- Use comments for discussion, not edits on top of other people's text
- Record contributions as you go with CRediT
- Put the link in every meeting agenda so nobody has to hunt for the document
